transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of ML, Astra Works), Jonas (CTO), Leah (DevOps)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Liam, our SE. Quick check — can everyone hear ok?
[00:06] Priya (Astra): Yes, hearing you. Thanks for the time.
[00:10] Jonas (Astra): Yep good to go.
[00:12] Liam (Redwood SE): Great. I'll give a very quick run through of the PLG quickstart flow and then we can jump into your specific questions — free credits, time to first token, things like that.

[00:32] Liam: So high level, Redwood's hosted API is basically self-serve — you sign up, you get free credits, a key, and you can hit text generation, chat, embeddings right away. We typically see customers do 'time-to-first-token' in under 10 minutes for a dev to make a call and see a response, provided they have minimal network setup. The quickstart repo and SDKs are in the deck I shared.
[00:48] Priya: Nice. So when you say free credits, is that applied to hosted only or does it cover Dedicated trials? We're trying to understand how quickly our product folks can prototype without procurement.

[01:05] Maya: Good question. The free credits are for the hosted API — it's PLG-friendly. For Dedicated or Private we do usually set up a pilot contract; we can give trial credits against a dedicated trial but that typically needs a short contract. For initial experimentation though the hosted API is the fastest path.

[01:24] Jonas: Ok — we're a small eng org. Our main concerns are latency for real-time assistant and data residency. We can't send PII to third-party services without some controls. How do folks handle that?

[01:40] Liam: Totally — two axes there. Latency: hosted is typically lowest-friction but latency depends on region and model choice. For 8k context models we're seeing p50 latencies in the 100-250ms per token range on optimized models; larger seqs or higher temps change that. We also do routing by region so requests from EU can hit EU regions.

[02:05] Priya: 100-250ms per token, is that end-to-end or just generation time on the GPU? Because our SLA target for interactive UI is sub 500ms for short replies.

[02:18] Liam: That's generation time on the runtime side; network + client overhead adds of course. For short replies (<= 60 tokens) many customers can hit under 500ms total if they use streaming and a smaller model. We'll send a baseline benchmark that shows p50/p95 numbers for the models we recommend.

[02:38] Leah (Astra): On the data residency piece — do you have a Private option that we can run in our VPC? We have to keep logs and raw user content inside our network for now.

[02:48] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane and on-prem options. We also have Dedicated which is single-tenant GPU pools with data isolation. For strict residency we usually recommend Private (VPC or on-prem), for predictable throughput Dedicated can work.

[03:05] Jonas: What's the onboarding timeline for Private? We're trying to plan ramp.

[03:11] Liam: Onboarding to Private can take a bit longer — usually 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and if you want on-prem. Dedicated is 2–4 weeks if it's a reserved capacity arrangement. Hosted is immediate. For most teams we suggest starting hosted for validation then moving to Dedicated or Private for production.

[03:30] Priya: That fits our thinking — prototype on hosted, then pivot. A couple of security checks: SOC 2, SSO, audit logs, encryption at rest, KMS — do you support all of these?

[03:42] Maya: Yes — Hosted is SOC 2 compliant and we support SSO/SAML and RBAC on the Console. We have audit logs, and for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. We'll attach our security pack (SOC2/ISO summary, pen test notes, SSO guide) in the follow-up.

[03:58] Jonas: Great. How about model control and rolling backwards — if a rollout degrades quality?

[04:06] Liam: Our Console supports version pinning, canary routes, and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. We also have eval hooks so you can tie regressions to prompt sets and get alerts. For short pilots we recommend pinning to a known good model to avoid surprises.

[04:25] Priya: For cost we want to understand token economics. Are there tools to estimate cost per request and batching options?

[04:34] Maya: Yes — Redwood Optimize offers batching and caching recommendations. In the Console you get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route stats. For the quickstart you can enable prefix caching which reduces repeated prompt costs. We'll include an example cost sheet.

[04:50] Leah: Any gotchas around API keys and secrets in dev? We typically have CICD pipelines and want short-lived creds.

[04:57] Liam: You can create scoped API keys in Console and rotate them. For hosted customers we also support short-lived creds and integrations with common CI secret managers. For Private, you manage keys via your KMS.

[05:12] Maya: Quick demo offer — we can run a 30 minute session where Liam walks through the quickstart, shows creating an API key, a sample call and streaming. Would that be useful?

[05:20] Priya: Yes please. That'd help our engs get comfortable.

[05:24] Jonas: Also, can you run a quick latency test against our sample prompts? We want to see p95 for typical 128–512 token replies.

[05:33] Liam: Absolutely — share the prompt set and we'll run a baseline on the recommended hosted model and return a CSV with p50/p95 and token counts. We'll also test streaming vs non-streaming.

[05:45] Priya: Perfect. Two more quick items — does Redwood support structured tool calling or function calling? Our assistant will call internal microservices.

[05:55] Liam: Yes we support function/tool calling and structured output; SDKs include typed helpers. For privacy you can restrict tool outputs and redact logs.

[06:05] Leah: Any PCI or HIPAA considerations? We're not doing card processing now but may have healthcare customers.

[06:13] Maya: We do have HIPAA offerings as a part of the Private deployment and additional controls for auditability. We can share the compliance matrix in the follow-up.

[06:22] Priya: Thanks — that's very helpful. I'd like to talk about a quick pilot plan: we want to spin up a dev team, run 2–3 day integration and then a week-long performance run to understand production costs. What do you recommend?

[06:35] Liam: Start with hosted using free credits and the quickstart repo, get time-to-first-token under 1 hour. Then define 10–20 prompts that represent production. We'll run the benchmark and propose model/quantization recommendations. If results look good we can scope a Dedicated pilot for predictable throughput.

[06:52] Jonas: That aligns. What's the typical cost delta between hosted and Dedicated? Ballpark.

[06:58] Maya: Hosted is pure usage pricing; Dedicated is reserved capacity — you get lower per-token costs at a commit but there's a monthly reservation. We'll send a ballpark pricing matrix — typical savings depend on usage profile but can be 20–40% for sustained high throughput.

[07:17] Priya: Ok. Can you also include runbook items for rate limiting and fallback if capacity spikes? We want graceful degradation.

[07:25] Liam: Yes — Redwood Console supports per-route rate limits and can automatically fallback to smaller models or cached responses. We'll include config examples in the runbook we share.

[07:36] Maya: Quick recap and next steps: we will send the PLG quickstart guide, free credits link, security pack (SOC2/ISO/SSO), a baseline benchmarking plan and a pricing matrix. Liam will schedule the 30-min demo with your engs and run the latency benchmark once you share prompts. Priya, you'll share sample prompts and success criteria.

[07:58] Priya: Sounds good. One ask — if we hit blockers on sending data to hosted during the pilot (legal), can we fast-track Dedicated trial?

[08:06] Maya: Yes — we have a short pilot contract for Dedicated trials and can escalate procurement. We'll include contacts for sales ops in the follow-up.

[08:15] Jonas: Great. Any final questions from your side?

[08:18] Liam: No, just timeline — can we aim to have the demo by next Tuesday?

[08:23] Priya: Tuesday works for us.

[08:25] Maya: Okay we'll propose times in the follow-up calendar invite.

[08:30] Jonas: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the clear plan.

[08:33] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the materials today.

[08:36] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription with occasional mis-hearings and run-ons; proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., KMS spelled out).
